label: Exponential improvement continuing
rationale: The best 80% METR time horizon reached 32.3 min (GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, Nov 2025), growing at a ~7-month doubling rate long-run and possibly ~4 months in 2024–2025. Caveat: METR's RCT found experienced developers 19% slower with AI tools, so benchmark gains do not yet translate to real-world productivity.

label: Approaching
rationale: No verified case meets the strict criteria (solo founder, $10M ARR, <10 hrs/week oversight); Magnific AI is at $10M ARR with 2 people and several AI-heavy solo founders are at ~$3M ARR. Current examples show AI as a coding accelerator, not an autonomous business operator.

label: Distant
rationale: The largest confirmed AI-generated patch merged into Linux is ~50 lines (in 6.15, undisclosed and buggy), 200× short of the 10k-line target. Major projects (Gentoo, NetBSD, Git, QEMU) ban or restrict AI code, and AI is adopted only in auxiliary maintenance roles.

label: Distant (structurally blocked)
rationale: All major journals (Nature, Science, Cell, JAMA/Lancet/BMJ) prohibit AI authorship, so the barrier is policy and accountability rather than capability. The closest approach, Sakana AI Scientist-v2's ICLR workshop paper, was accepted and then withdrawn.

label: Ahead: 80% horizon 185.9 min (Apr 2026); doubling ~4.1 mo in 2 yrs vs ~7 mo benchmark (tier 3)
rationale: The release-cohort METR 80% time horizon rose from 4.42 min (frontier at 2024-09-30) to 185.91 min (Claude Mythos Preview early, released 2026-04-07), a 42x gain over the 2-year window across 9 new frontier points: a log-linear fit gives a doubling time of 4.1 months (95% CI 3.4-5.1), and the endpoint ratio gives 4.45 months. That beats the tier-3 benchmark of sustaining METR's long-run ~7-month doubling, and it is faster than the previous window 2022-09-30..2024-09-30 (0.26 -> 4.42 min, endpoint doubling 5.9 months), so the status is green (Ahead). The result survives dropping the latest, wide-CI point (4.4 months), and it already absorbs the ~6 months since April 2026 with no new frontier.

label: Progressing: solo AI-heavy firms ~$3-3.5M ARR; <10 h/week oversight unevidenced; ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No verified achievement event shows a single-person company at $10M ARR with <10 hours/week of oversight. The closest solo cases are about $3M (Pieter Levels, corrected record) and Base44's $3.5M ARR before its $80M exit (legacy); the $10M-plus small-team cases are 2-person Magnific or the largely pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith (legacy, non-primary), with no oversight data. That is measurable progress on the revenue half at ~1/3 of the target, and OpenView finds AI-native startups 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR within 12 months, but nothing evidences the <10 h/week clause, and there is no programme or non-proponent corroboration that would support a <=5-year ETA. The credible ETA is 5-10 years, so the status is yellow.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity (solo-company ARR) with a credible ETA of 5-10 years; not green (no funded programme, precursor at relevant scale or non-proponent corroboration of the oversight clause); not achieved (no verified achievement event)

basis.path: AI-leveraged solo businesses (Pieter Levels ~$3M revenue; Base44 $3.5M ARR, legacy) and tiny AI teams at $10M ARR (Magnific, 2 people, legacy); AI-native startups 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR in 12 months (OpenView)
blockers: Technical/operational: no evidence of any company at this revenue run with <10 h/week of human oversight (reliability/agency of autonomous operation)
Data: revenue and headcount figures are self-reported or secondary (LinkedIn, tinyteams), and oversight hours are never reported

It gave no ETA, path or blockers basis, and it cited records since superseded: the Levels figure was corrected from '$3.1M ARR' to about $3M revenue, and the OpenView record was re-verified. label: Distant: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15, human-submitted); no path to a 10k-line AI patch
rationale: The only verified precursor is LWN's report that a patch merged for Linux 6.15 was entirely LLM-written and posted without disclosure; re-verification removed the earlier size and bug details, and it was human-submitted. There is no series on the size of accepted AI-generated patches to extrapolate and no funded programme aiming at AI-submitted large patches. Torvalds positions AI for maintaining, not writing, kernel code, and critical-infra projects ban AI code (Gentoo, QEMU) or require a human in the loop (LLVM), which cuts against an 'AI-submitted' patch. With no evidenced path, the status is red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: no evidenced path (no series on the milestone's own quantity and no programme or precursor at relevant scale), so the ETA is not evidenced within 10 years
basis.eta: >10 years / not evidenced: a single small, human-submitted LLM-written patch is the only precursor, and there is no trend on accepted AI-patch size to extrapolate
basis.path: None evidenced. Precursor: undisclosed fully LLM-written patch merged in Linux 6.15 (LWN, Jun 2025). Context (legacy): kernel TAB 'generated-content' disclosure guidelines proposed Nov 2025; Levin's RFC for AI-assistant config files, Jul 2025
blockers: Policy: Gentoo and QEMU bar AI-generated contributions and NetBSD bans them (legacy); LLVM requires a human in the loop, which conflicts with an 'AI-submitted' patch
Social/process: maintainers position AI for maintenance rather than authorship (Torvalds, Dec 2025); 10k-line diffs face heavy review burden
Definitional: 'AI-submitted' excludes the human-submitted AI-written patches that are the only precursors
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-linux-kernel-patch) scored the distance to goal ('~50 lines, 200x short of 10k'), which STATUS.md reports but never scores. The ~50-line and 'buggy' details it relied on were removed on re-verification. It gave no ETA, path or blockers basis, and it cited records since superseded (Gentoo, QEMU, Torvalds, LWN). Under v1 red rests on the absence of any evidenced path (Distant), with the policy obstacles named.

label: Blocked: Nature/Science bar AI authorship (policy); best precursor an ICLR workshop paper, withdrawn
rationale: The milestone requires AI credited as primary author in Nature/Science, and both journals' policies bar AI authorship: 'LLMs do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria' and 'AI tools cannot be authors' (legacy record, used as context). That is a structural policy block whatever the technical readiness. The best verified precursor is Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 paper, which passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop but was withdrawn before publication because the community had not decided whether to publish AI-generated manuscripts. Recognitions such as the 2024 chemistry Nobel went to humans, so no evidence moves the block, and the status is red (Blocked).

basis.rule: Milestone red: structurally blocked (policy: the target journals prohibit AI authorship), whatever the technical readiness
basis.eta: >10 years / blocked: it cannot happen until Nature or Science changes its authorship policy, and no evidence shows such a change underway
basis.path: Technical precursor only: AI Scientist-v2 paper passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop, then was withdrawn (Sakana, Mar 2025). Context: 36% of cancer-paper abstracts AI-generated with 9% disclosure (legacy), i.e. AI contributes uncredited
blockers: Policy: Nature Portfolio and Science/AAAS (plus Cell, ICMJE journals) prohibit crediting AI as an author (legacy record)

It misstated the Sakana withdrawal as 'per a prior ethical agreement' (corrected: withdrawn under the experiment protocol because the community is undecided) and cited records since superseded (Sakana, AlphaFold Nobel). It also gave no ETA, path or blockers basis.

label: Progressing: best AI-era solo firms ~$3M/yr (30% of $10M); <10 h/wk oversight unproven; ETA ~2030
rationale: No verified case shows a one-person company at $10M ARR with <10 h/week of oversight. The best AI-era solo figures are ~$3M (Pieter Levels; HeadshotPro, legacy), and a pre-AI solo firm already exceeds $10M (BuiltWith, legacy), so the binding clause is oversight. It maps onto the METR 80% horizon: about a work-week (2,400 min) of autonomous work is needed vs 185.91 min today, 12.9x or 3.7 doublings plus ~1.6 for messy business operations, which at a 5-month doubling and a 1.5-year ramp to disclosure gives p50 ~2030 (p10 2028, p90 2034). The median is within 5 years, but there is no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale and no independent corroboration of the oversight clause, so the status is yellow, not green.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on a driver the milestone is tied to (METR 80% horizon) with median ETA <= 5 years, but the path lacks green's conditions (funded programme, precursor at relevant scale, non-proponent corroboration); not achieved (no verified achievement event)

eta.method: driver trend (METR 80% horizon, exponential) + structural lag (revenue ramp and disclosure); reference class cross-check
eta.calc: Revenue clause: best AI-era solo ~$3M (Levels, 2025-01-01-pieter-levels-3m-arr-rv; HeadshotPro $3M ARR, legacy tinyteams) -> 10/3 = 3.3x (1.74 doublings); pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith $14M/yr (legacy) shows the level is attainable. Oversight clause: <10 h/wk needs agents to carry ~1 work-week between check-ins, an 80% horizon of ~40 h = 2,400 min. metr-80-horizon-by-release 185.91 min (2026-04-07) -> 12.9x = 3.69 doublings, plus messiness x3 (1.58 doublings) = 5.28 doublings x 5 mo (central; current-window endpoint 4.45, long-run 6.4) = 26.4 mo -> capability 2028-06, plus 1.5 yr ramp/disclosure -> 2030.0. p10: (3.69+0.58) x 3.5 mo = 15 mo -> 2027-07, +0.5 yr -> 2028. p90: (3.69+2.58) x 9 mo = 56.5 mo -> 2030-12, +3 yr -> 2034. Ramp check: AI-native startups 8x likelier to hit $10M ARR within 12 months (OpenView); Base44 $3.5M run-rate within ~6 months (not evidenced as one-person).
eta.cruxes: Earlier: a verified 1-person company at >=$10M ARR disclosing low founder hours; an 80% horizon >= ~8 h by mid-2027; AI-era solo businesses passing $5M. Later: horizon doubling slowing past ~8 months; agent reliability failures in customer-facing operations (cf. 95% of GenAI pilots falling short); legal/compliance duties that need human hours; oversight hours never disclosed, so the milestone cannot be verified.

basis.path: Driver: METR 80% horizon (42x in 2 years, 4.45-month doubling) is the proxy for <10 h/week oversight, because it measures how long agents work unsupervised at 80% reliability. Revenue: AI-era solo firms ~$3M (Levels, HeadshotPro); BuiltWith 1-person $14M/yr (pre-AI); Magnific $10M ARR with 2 people (legacy); AI-native firms 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR in 12 months. The proxy is uncertain because business operations are messier than METR tasks, which is why p90 is wide.
blockers: Technical/operational: no evidence of any company at this revenue with <10 h/week of oversight (agent reliability over week-long, customer-facing work)
Data: revenue and headcount figures are self-reported or secondary, and oversight hours are never reported; a gather request should look for disclosed founder hours
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status stays yellow. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-the-10m-solopreneur, v1) gave the ETA as a restated status band ('5-10 years (~2031-2036)'), which RUBRIC.md §4.1/§6 rules out. It had no median, no range and no arithmetic, and it did not tie the oversight clause to a driver. It also treated Base44 as a solo case, but the re-verified record (2025-01-01-base44-solo-80m-exit-rv) does not support one-person. Tying the oversight clause to the METR 80% horizon gives p50 ~2030 (within 5 years); the status stays yellow only because the path lacks green's three conditions.

label: Progressing: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15); 10k lines ~484x the 80% horizon; ETA ~2031
rationale: The only verified precursor is a fully LLM-written patch merged for Linux 6.15, human-submitted and of unstated size, but the milestone ties to the METR 80% horizon, which grew 42x in two years. A substantive 10k-line patch series is ~1,500 h of expert work, 484x today's 185.91-min horizon: at 8.9 doublings plus one for real-world messiness and a 5-month doubling, the capability arrives ~2030, and a 1-year review floor gives p50 ~2031 (p10 2028, p90 2038). Gentoo, QEMU and NetBSD bar AI code and LLVM requires a human in the loop, but Linux has no ban and 'or equivalent critical infra' needs only one accepting project, so this is a risk rather than a structural block. The path lacks a programme, a precursor at scale and corroboration, so the status is yellow (Progressing).

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the driver it is tied to (METR 80% horizon) with median ETA <= 10 years; the path lacks green's conditions (no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale, no corroboration); not blocked, because no ban covers Linux and 'or equivalent critical infra' allows any accepting project

eta.method: driver trend (METR 80% horizon, exponential) + structural floor (review/acceptance of a 10k-line series); reference class cross-check
eta.calc: Effort of a substantive 10k-line kernel series ~500 / 1,500 / 4,000 h (3 person-months to 2 person-years). metr-80-horizon-by-release 185.91 min (2026-04-07). Central: 90,000/185.91 = 484x = 8.92 doublings, +1 net (messiness +1.5, agentic decomposition -0.5) = 9.92 x 5 mo = 49.6 mo -> 2030-05, +1 yr review -> 2031.4. p10: 500 h -> 161x = 7.33 doublings x 3.5 mo = 25.7 mo -> 2028-05, +0.5 yr -> 2028.9; a mechanical treewide 10k+-line diff could come earlier -> 2028. p90: 4,000 h -> 1,291x = 10.33 doublings +2 = 12.33 x 9 mo = 111 mo -> 2035-07, +2 yr -> 2037.5, plus policy risk -> 2038. Doubling: current-window endpoint 4.45 mo, long-run 6.4 mo (2019-2026). Reference class (background): Rust-for-Linux's ~12k-line base took ~20 months from RFC to merge.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an agent-authored multi-thousand-line series merged into any critical project; kernel docs (Hansen's generated-content guidelines) explicitly allowing agent-submitted patches with disclosure; an 80% horizon >= 1 work-week by 2027. Later: the kernel or other projects requiring human submitters / Signed-off-by for AI code; horizon doubling slowing past ~8 months; mergeable-quality rates staying far below benchmark pass rates.

basis.path: Driver: METR 80% horizon (4.42 -> 185.91 min, 2024-10..2026-04), the RUBRIC §4.1's own mapping for an AI-written 10k-line patch. Precursor: fully LLM-written patch merged for Linux 6.15 (LWN, Jun 2025; human-submitted, size not stated). Process: TAB generated-content guidelines and an in-tree AI-assistant config RFC (legacy); Torvalds a 'huge believer' in AI for maintenance; >25% of Google's new code AI-written. Uncertainty: METR tasks are cleaner than kernel work (the METR RCT found devs 19% slower), so messiness is added in the calc.
blockers: Policy (risk, not a full block): Gentoo and QEMU bar AI-generated contributions, NetBSD bans them (legacy), and LLVM requires a human in the loop; Linux has no ban
Definitional risk: 'AI-submitted' excludes the human-submitted AI-written patches that are the only precursors; if critical projects insist on human submitters, the milestone is blocked
Process: 10k-line series face months to years of review (structural floor in the ETA)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status red -> yellow. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-the-linux-kernel-patch, v1) called the milestone red ('Distant: no path') because there was no series on accepted AI-patch size. RUBRIC.md v2 §4.1 step 2 says a missing series is a gap to work around by tying the milestone to a driver, and it names METR horizons as the driver for exactly this milestone. It gave '>10 years / not evidenced' instead of a forecast. It also counted project-specific bans (Gentoo, QEMU) as obstacles to a milestone that any critical-infra project can satisfy. On the driver, p50 is ~2031, inside 10 years, so the status is yellow.

label: Blocked: Nature/Science bar AI authors (policy); best AI paper an ICLR workshop one; ETA ~2037
rationale: Nature says LLMs 'do not currently satisfy' its authorship criteria and Science says AI 'may not be listed as authors' (re-verified on a 2026-03 capture), a structural policy block whatever the technical readiness. On capability, the best precursor is Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 ICLR-workshop paper (withdrawn). A Nature-level paper (~4,000 h of work) is 230x the 17.4-h METR 50% horizon, about 2031 with research messiness and review at a 5-month doubling. Adding a ~6-year policy lag (authorship rules built on accountability have held since 2023) gives p50 ~2037 (p10 2030, p90 never), so the status is red (Blocked, policy) and the median is >10 years too.

basis.rule: Milestone red: structurally blocked (policy: Nature and Science do not allow AI to be listed as author), whatever the technical readiness; the median ETA is also > 10 years

eta.method: driver trend (METR 50% horizon, exponential) for capability + structural floor (journal review) + policy lag judged from the reference class of authorship norms
eta.calc: Capability: a Nature/Science paper ~2,000 / 4,000 / 10,000 h of work; one acceptance with best-of-many attempts, so the 50% horizon applies: metr-50-horizon-by-release 1,044.78 min (2026-04-07; 20.33 -> 1,044.78 over 2 yr, endpoint doubling 4.22 mo, long-run 6.39 mo). Central 240,000/1,044.78 = 230x = 7.84 doublings, +2 for research messiness/novelty = 9.84 x 5 mo = 49.2 mo -> 2030-05, +0.75 yr review -> 2031.1. p10 capability: 115x = 6.84 +1 = 7.84 x 3.5 mo -> 2028-07 -> 2029.3; p90: 574x = 9.17 +3 = 12.17 x 9 mo -> 2035-05 -> 2036.4. Policy lag after capability: central 6 yr -> 2037.1; p10: a quick opening (e.g. an AI-generated-research track) -> 2030; p90: rule never changes -> null. Context: AlphaProof's Nature paper credits human authors (knowledge-beyond 2025-11-01-alphaproof-nature-rv); 36% of cancer abstracts are AI-generated with 9% disclosed (legacy).
eta.cruxes: Earlier: Nature or Science revising authorship policy (dropping 'currently'-style hedges in AI's favour) or piloting AI-credited papers; an AI-generated paper accepted at a main-track top venue (not a workshop). Later: policies hardening; AI-originated results continuing to be published only under human authors (as with AlphaProof); horizon growth slowing on open-ended research tasks.

basis.path: Capability proxy: METR 50% horizon (17.4 h, doubling ~4-6 months), because it measures how long an agent can work autonomously on hard tasks. Research is more open-ended than METR tasks, hence +2 doublings. Precursors: AI Scientist-v2 workshop paper passed peer review (Mar 2025, withdrawn); IMO gold (Gemini Deep Think); AlphaEvolve results (legacy). The policy half has no trend: the stance is unchanged since 2023.
blockers: Policy (structural): Nature Portfolio says LLMs do not currently satisfy its authorship criteria; Science journals say AI may not be listed as authors or coauthors (2025-01-01-journals-prohibit-ai-authorship-rv)
Policy/community: the only peer-reviewed fully AI-generated paper was withdrawn because the community had not decided whether to publish such work
Capability: no AI-generated paper has yet been accepted at a main-track top venue
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-the-nature-author, v1) gave the ETA as '>10 years / blocked' with no median, range or arithmetic. RUBRIC.md v2 §4.1/§6 requires a reasoned forecast even when the target is blocked, with the capability driver (METR 50% horizon) and the policy lag modelled separately. It also cited the legacy journals-policy record, which has since been superseded by the re-verified 2025-01-01-journals-prohibit-ai-authorship-rv. The forecast puts p50 at ~2037, so red holds on both the block and the >10-year median.
